searches.note: Twenty eight searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's. Six were restricted to a house's or a body's own domain (taylor.pt, grahams-port.com with symington.com, quintadonoval.com, sandeman.com with sogrape.com, sogrape.com, ivdp.pt) and are read as primary through their summaries; eight kept the house's own domain out so that the second source would be independent (Taylor's, Graham's twice, Noval four times, Sandeman). One Noval search returned nothing on the subject and was spent again on the house's and the trade's domains. The two shared searches are the IVDP's rules for the special categories and the label of an aged tawny. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the open web, with the house's own domain kept out, for the second source of each date and person, then to the houses' own pages and sheets for their own dates, sites and methods, then to the IVDP for the rules.

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail was found in no source of this check and rested on one of the author's secondary sources or a sheet hosted by a merchant, it was cut or said with less (the double walled vessel, the two dozen estates and the mother of the poor, the eighteen months in vats and the sea air at Graham's, the destemming and the two or three months open at Sandeman, the family at Sandeman's head until 1952).

Facts of a house's own history told on its own pages stand, hedged as the house's account where the story tells them so; a person is named only with dates in two sources (Dona Antónia Adelaide Ferreira, Fernando Nicolau de Almeida), and every other founder, partner or heir stays described.

Sources whose title or address names a living writer, or a writer's own site, were met among the results but are cited neither in the fragment nor here; the fragment's sources were left as the author wrote them, and the sources of this check are listed per change and per record under extraSources.

tested: 1692 and the Bearsley family, trading first in the red wine of the Minho: Wein.plus and a Portugal visitor guide give 1692 and the English merchant Bearsley, one of them the lean red wine of the Minho. Confirmed; the founder stays described, as no dates were found.

1744, the first Douro property near Régua: Wikipedia and a Port guide give the purchase near Régua in 1744 by a Bearsley of the second or third generation, called Salgueiral in some accounts and Lugar das Lages in another. Confirmed as the record words it, which names neither.

Vargellas bought between 1893 and 1896, two of its three parts from the railway's contractor: the house's own page (Taylor rebuilds estate) names the railway's general contractor as the seller of Lower and Middle Vargellas in 1893, and a Port database and the house's importer give the three properties joined between 1893 and 1896. Confirmed.

The Yeatman partner who rebuilt Vargellas after phylloxera, and the wine good enough for the Vintage blend by 1908: the house's page gives both, and a Port database names 1908 and 1912 as years Vargellas gave a large part of the declared blend. Confirmed; the partner stays described.
Terra Feita bought in 1974, its wine bought since the previous century: the house's importer and a Port guide give 1974 and supply since the 1890s. Confirmed.

Declaration on 23 April of the second year: the house's own declaration page, Decanter and a trade paper give St George's Day, 23 April, and the two winters in vat before the decision. Confirmed; the card now names the day.

The making: the house's 2017 page gives about twenty months in wood, and its winery and method pages give foot treading in granite lagares for all the house's Vintage Ports and fortification about halfway through fermentation. Confirmed.
Taylor Fladgate as the name of some markets: the house's United States importer sells it as Taylor Fladgate. Confirmed.
The questions: one key each, four methods and four spans of years; sound.
The rules: nobody living named; no price, no score, nothing volatile; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: 1820, two brothers in textiles, twenty seven barrels in payment of a debt: Nickolls and Perks, a merchant's history and others give 1820, the textile trade and twenty seven barrels, pipes or casks by different accounts. Confirmed, told as the house's account.

1882, a young Scot from Glasgow: the Symingtons' own Graham's page and outside accounts give the forebear's arrival in 1882 to work for the Grahams, and his own shipping firm after. Confirmed; he stays described, as his dates were in one source only.

1890, Malvedos bought: the Symingtons' page and outside accounts give 1890, one 1880; the Symingtons' page says cornerstone ever since, while outside accounts have the quinta bought back only in 1982. The table's has been its heart since 1890 claimed a continuity the sources dispute and is reworded.
1970, the grandsons' purchase: two accounts give 1970 and the third generation. Confirmed.

Robotic lagares at Malvedos: the Symingtons' winery page gives three modern lagares installed in 2000, a magazine's account of the 2000 Vintage calls it the first Vintage made with them, and Decanter has one granite lagar kept. The year now stands in the making and the story; the share trodden by foot in some years was in none and is cut.

Time in wood: the house's pages give the lodge of 1890 where all its wines are aged, and its LBV page gives two years in cask for a Vintage; the record's eighteen months in wooden vats and the sea air were in no source of this check. Changed.

The grapes and sites: a magazine's note on the 2017 Vintage, quoted by merchants, gives Touriga Franca from Malvedos, Touriga Nacional from Vila Velha and Vale de Malhadas, old vines at Tua and a tenth of Sousão. Confirmed.
The questions: the wine question's key is reworded to match the making; one key each, four places of ageing and four years. Sound after the change.
The rules: nobody living named (the Symingtons are named as a family of shippers, as the plan names them); no price, no score; British; no dash. Sound.

changed.was: The grapes are trodden in the lagares of the house's winery at Malvedos, robotic ones built to copy the human foot, with a share trodden by foot in some years, and grape spirit stops the fermentation. The wine spends about eighteen months in wooden vats at the house's lodge of 1890 in Vila Nova de Gaia, cooled by the sea air, and is bottled by the third year after the harvest, as the rules require.
changed.now: The grapes are trodden at the house's winery at Malvedos in robotic lagares built to copy the human foot, installed in 2000, and grape spirit stops the fermentation. The wine then spends about two years in wood at the house's lodge of 1890 in Vila Nova de Gaia, where all its wines are aged, and is bottled by the third year after the harvest, as the rules require.
changed.why: The Symingtons' winery page dates the lagares to 2000; the house's pages give the lodge where all its wines age and two years in cask for a Vintage; foot treading in some years, eighteen months, vats and the sea air were in no source of this check.

changed.why: Outside accounts have Malvedos bought back only in 1982 after the Symington purchase of 1970, so an unbroken heart since 1890 is not safe; the purchase year and its place in the blend are.

tested: 1715 in the land registers: Antique Wines and a winery guide give the name's first appearance in 1715. Confirmed as the record tells it, a first record and not a founding.

1894, a Port shipper who replanted after phylloxera, and his son in law who widened the terraces for the sun: two outside accounts name both and the broader terraces with more sun. Confirmed; both stay described, with no dates found.

1931: a Port database and two outside accounts give few shippers declaring in the depression, with the 1927 declared by some thirty shippers and unsold, and Noval's reputation made by its 1931. Confirmed; the 1931 Nacional as the first is in one account only and the record does not claim it.

1981 and 1993: two outside accounts give the Gaia fire of 1981 destroying the lodge, bottling plant, offices and records, the new cellar on the quinta from 1982 and the stocks moved there, and the sale by the family to AXA Millésimes in 1993. The fire is reworded to match.
1996 and 2007: the house's own Nacional page and Wine-Searcher give the 1996 Nacional declared when the rest of the estate was not, and 2007 Noval declared without Nacional. Confirmed.

The making, the grapes and the window: the house's Nacional sheets give foot treading in the quinta's granite lagares, eighteen months in 2500 litre casks of oak and chestnut, a field blend naming Touriga Nacional, Touriga Francesa, Tinto Cão, Tinta Roriz and Sousão, five to a hundred years after bottling, and serving at 15 to 17 degrees Celsius. Confirmed and set more exactly; the serve keeps the Codex's 16 to 18 for Vintage Port, as the brief asks.
The questions: one key each, four reasons and four years; the 1927 distractor is explained. Sound.
The rules: nobody living named; AXA Millésimes is told as the buyer of 1993; no price, no score; British; no dash. Sound after the table's exceptional became the house's own judgement.

Dona Antónia Adelaide Ferreira (1811 to 1896), widowed at thirty three, the house of 1751, Sogrape in 1987: Wikipedia and others give her dates and her widowhood of 1844, the house's founding in 1751, and her descendants' ownership until 1987; her estates grew in her time. The two dozen estates and the mother of the poor were in no source of this check and are cut.

Sites and grapes: Sogrape gives the greater part of the blend from Quinta da Leda's vineyards and grapes from different altitudes in the Douro Superior, and Touriga Franca and Touriga Nacional leading its Leda and Reserva Especial reds. The sites are reworded to its words.
The questions: one key each, four styles and four years; the story stem no longer reads as a claim of a first. Sound after the change.
The rules: the head winemaker since 2007 is living and not named; Sogrape is told as the buyer of 1987; no price, no score; the table's exceptional became the house's own judgement; British; no dash.

Confirmed; the founder stays described, his death year being in one source only.
Port and sherry from the start: outside accounts give him trading in both from the coffee house. Confirmed.

The lodges at Gaia and the old tawny of the mid nineteenth century: the house's history page gives both, with no date for the lodges; Sogrape's tourism page has wine ageing in the building since 1811. Both are now told as the house's account.

The Don of 1928: the house's arts page gives the artist at the Lochend printing company's studio in 1928, the Portuguese student's cape and the Spanish hat; one poster seller has the figure named only in 1935. Confirmed as the record tells it; the artist stays described, his birth year being given two ways.

1952, Seagram, 2002: Wein.plus gives the change of 1952 into a stock corporation, Wikipedia a family business until Seagram in 1979, the house 1980, and two accounts Sogrape in 2002. The family's end in 1952 is cut, and Seagram's year is now given as accounts differ.

The grapes and making: Sogrape's importer lists the five grapes and an awards entry three of them, neither with a share; the house's page gives the traditional Porto method; no source of this check gave the destemming, the controlled temperature or the two or three months open. Cut or said with less.
The serve and the label: a tasting note says serve chilled; secondary accounts give the bottling year on an aged tawny's label. The 12 to 14 degrees stands with the Codex's service quiz.
The questions: one key each, four answers of one kind and four years. Sound.
The rules: the seventh generation family member who shares the founder's name is living and not named; no price, no score; British; no dash. Sound.
